redeemer-bible-church-spotsylvania.assessment: Redeemer Bible Church is a recent and highly promising church plant out of Spotswood Baptist. It is solidly grounded in conservative evangelical theology, formally affirming the Baptist Faith & Message (2000). The church is led by a well-educated pastor, Victor (Vic) Carpenter, who holds a Ph.D. from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Their leadership structure includes a plurality of male elders, and they have dedicated ministries for men, women, and children. MOOP-context note (Adam Johns, 2026): Adam attended both Redeemer Bible Spotsy and Stafford and characterizes the network as "splants" from his home church Spotswood Baptist — the new chain catered to Spotswood members who were "more Calvinist leaning" than Spotswood's SBC mainstream. The Calvinist/Reformed Baptist leaning is theologically substantive (more rigorous soteriology) but the church-network history is partly a tactical accommodation rather than a pure missional plant. Worth understanding as inheritor of Spotswood's baseline orthodoxy + Reformed-Baptist refinement.

redemption-hill-church-dc.assessment: Redemption Hill Church is a doctrinally serious Gospel-centered church plant in the heart of Capitol Hill DC, launched in 2011 by Pastor Bill Riedel. The church's self-description — 'gospel-centered worship, gospel-shaped community, gospel-driven mission' — maps directly onto what a disciple-making, Great Commission church should look like. Strong alignment with 9Marks ecclesiology means healthy membership practices, expository preaching, and elder-led governance. Two services (9AM and 5PM) serve the Capitol Hill community of government workers, military, and young professionals. For USMC Ministries, this is exactly the kind of city-center church plant that models what healthy church planting looks like in a mission field context. Smaller congregation means deeper community possible.

refuge-church-ogden.assessment: Refuge Church in Ogden, Utah is a Reformed congregation led by pastor Brian Sauvé — a nationally known author and teacher on biblical masculinity, patriarchal households, and Reformed theology. The church holds strong complementarian convictions and preaches expository, confessional Christianity in the heart of LDS-dominated Utah. Critics on Reddit have called it 'cult-like' for its emphasis on large families and women's roles — standard internet blowback against any church that takes the Bible seriously on gender. The 'Mark and Avoid' site flag (from April 2025) regarding Eric Conn should be investigated. The theological foundation is solid. For men in the Ogden area looking for a doctrinally serious, biblically masculine church culture in a difficult mission field — Refuge is one of the strongest options in the region. Verify current leadership stability before committing.

reston-bible-church.assessment: Reston Bible Church has 50+ years of consistent Bible-teaching ministry in Northern Virginia — founded 1975 by Mike Minter, whose legacy continues under Senior Teaching Pastor Jim Supp. The church is officially located in Dulles/Sterling (the Oakbrook Court address) though still widely known as 'Reston Bible.' RBC's stated purpose — 'know Christ and make Him known through biblical preaching, teaching, and authentic Christian community in Northern Virginia and around the world' — is a solid evangelical mission statement. Two Sunday services, community groups infrastructure, and a strong local/global mission orientation. For a man in the Reston, Herndon, Sterling, or Ashburn corridor, RBC is a proven, established option with deep community roots and consistent biblical teaching.

restoration-buffalo-sbc-amherst-ny.assessment: Restoration Church is a Reformed Baptist congregation in Amherst (Buffalo), New York, affiliated with the Southern Baptist Convention through the Frontier Baptist Association and led by Wes Walker — a founding elder who planted Aim Church in Alabama and returned to Buffalo in January 2025 to take the lead role. It holds Scripture as the only infallible Word of God, an orthodox high Christology, Reformed-Baptist soteriology (regeneration by the Spirit, believer’s baptism by immersion), and an elder-led government with membership by elder interview. An acquaintance of MOOP, a member there, reports that the preaching is expository — typically one book of the Bible at a time — and would rate the church green across all ten categories, while candidly noting the pastor could be bolder on some social topics. It earns green throughout.

As a brand-new GMC plant rather than a transitioned former UMC congregation, this church's identity is defined entirely by orthodox Wesleyan doctrine from inception — no legacy progressivism to unwind. The caution is typical GMC ambiguity on gender/elder policy (verify Mid Texas Conference stance) and the reality that small young plants often have less-developed men's ministries. Still, a green-eligible option for readers seeking a post-UMC-split orthodox Wesleyan church in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro.
